workflow: A loadable component uses a legacy initialization model that stores context-owned objects in process-global state.
The component is initialized inside an isolated execution context and creates objects and metadata associated with that context.
The context is torn down, but the global state has no per-context cleanup path and retains references to those objects.
Leak detection at process exit reports the retained object graph as unreclaimed memory instead of clean teardown.
summary: Legacy global component state survives isolated-context teardown
decision_reason: The failure mechanism materially matches the existing cluster: legacy shared component state outlives the lifecycle of an isolated execution context, preventing cleanup and producing leaks.
